# VFD Pump Control Narrative: Template and P-1102 Example

## Before you use this

**1. Batch framing.** Your speed reference comes from a batch system, so this plant is ISA-88 territory, not ISA-106. Treat each pump as an ISA-88 control module that a batch phase acquires and commands.
- The batch phase owns the procedural states (Running, Held, Aborted).
- The pump module owns only device states: Stopped, Starting, Running, Stopping, Faulted.
- Do not write phase logic in the pump narrative. The phase narrative references the pump module.

**2. The setpoint list needs a home.** This template refers to timeouts, speed clamps and debounce times. These belong in neither the I/O list nor the alarm database. Add a "Module Parameters" tab to the I/O list, with one row per parameter per module. The template refers to it as the **parameter list**.

**3. Class versus instance.** About 120 modules is enough to treat the VFD pump as a class:
- Sections 3 to 9 are fixed standard text. Engineers change only the `{{fields}}`.
- Test the standard behavior once per class at FAT, using a simulated pump.
- Test each instance only for its tags, interlocks and deviations.
- Any change to the fixed text is a deviation. Record it in Section 0.

---

## 1. Purpose and boundaries

- **Function:** {{one sentence: what the pump moves, from where, to where}}
- **Commanded by:** {{batch phase(s) / unit}}
- **Out of scope:** path valves (separate modules), CIP sequencing, phase logic, SIS functions.

| Interface | Tag / module | Direction | Signal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Source | {{tank / equipment}} | In | {{level switch / transmitter}} |
| Destination | {{tank / equipment}} | In | {{level switch / transmitter}} |
| Batch system | {{phase name}} | In / Out | Acquire, start, stop, speed reference, state, faults |
| VFD | {{VFD tag}} | In / Out | {{network / hardwired}} |
| {{other}} | | | |

## 2. Equipment and tags

The I/O list holds all ranges, engineering units and addresses. The alarm database holds all alarm limits. This table assigns roles only.

| Role | Tag |
|---|---|
| Pump / motor | {{tag}} |
| VFD | {{tag}} |
| Run command / run feedback | {{tag}} / {{tag}} |
| VFD fault / ready | {{tag}} / {{tag}} |
| Speed reference / speed feedback | {{tag}} / {{tag}} |
| Motor current | {{tag}} |
| Local disconnect status | {{tag, or "Not monitored"}} |
| Discharge pressure | {{tag, or "None"}} |
| Source low level | {{tag, or "None"}} |
| Destination high level | {{tag, or "None"}} |
| Other | {{tag}} |

**Parameter list entries.** Each one is required. Values live in the parameter list.

| Parameter | Use |
|---|---|
| `{{TAG}}.START_TMO` | Start feedback timeout |
| `{{TAG}}.STOP_TMO` | Stop feedback timeout |
| `{{TAG}}.SPD_MIN` / `.SPD_MAX` | Speed reference clamps |
| `{{TAG}}.SPD_START` | Speed reference during Starting |
| `{{TAG}}.SW_DEBOUNCE` | Level switch debounce |
| `{{TAG}}.PROOF_DLY` | Delay after run feedback before process checks apply |
| VFD accel / decel ramps | VFD parameter file, referenced by the parameter list |

## 3. Modes and states

### 3.1 Modes (ownership)

| Mode | Owner of start / stop / speed | Entry | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Program | Batch phase that acquired the module | Operator selects on faceplate | Default mode after commissioning |
| Operator | Operator, from the faceplate | Operator selects and confirms | For manual transfers and troubleshooting |
| Out of Service | None | Operator selects; module must be Stopped | Commands ignored; run output off |

The field disconnect is not a mode. The module reports it as a status (FR-{{TAG}}-019).

### 3.2 Device states

| State | Description | Entry permissives | Allowed exits |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stopped | Run command off, run feedback off | None | Starting, Faulted |
| Starting | Run command on, waiting for run feedback | All start permissives on the C&E chart are healthy | Running, Stopping, Faulted |
| Running | Run feedback on, speed follows the owner | Run feedback on within `START_TMO` | Stopping, Faulted |
| Stopping | Run command off, waiting for run feedback off | Stop command or loss of run request | Stopped, Faulted |
| Faulted | Run command off, latched | Any fault in Section 3.3 | Stopped (operator reset only) |

### 3.3 Transitions

| ID | From → To | Initiator | Condition | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Stopped → Starting | Owner | Start command, and all start permissives healthy | Program: automatic. Operator: operator |
| T2 | Starting → Running | Auto | Run feedback on within `START_TMO` | Automatic |
| T3 | Starting → Faulted | Auto | No run feedback in `START_TMO` (fail to start) | Automatic |
| T4 | Running → Stopping | Owner | Stop command | Program: automatic. Operator: operator |
| T5 | Stopping → Stopped | Auto | Run feedback off within `STOP_TMO` | Automatic |
| T6 | Stopping → Faulted | Auto | Run feedback still on after `STOP_TMO` (fail to stop) | Automatic |
| T7 | Any running state → Faulted | Auto | Interlock trip, VFD fault, uncommanded loss of run feedback, VFD comms loss | Automatic |
| T8 | Faulted → Stopped | Operator | Reset pushed, and all trip causes clear | Operator |
| T9 | Starting → Stopping | Owner | Stop command during Starting | Program: automatic. Operator: operator |

### 3.4 Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-{{TAG}}-001 | In Program mode, the module accepts start, stop and speed commands only from the acquiring batch phase. | FAT-S: send commands from the phase and from the faceplate. Only the phase commands take effect. |
| FR-{{TAG}}-002 | In Operator mode, the module accepts start, stop and speed commands only from the faceplate. | FAT-S |
| FR-{{TAG}}-003 | A mode change does not change the device state or the speed reference. | FAT-S: change mode while Running. Speed and state do not change. |
| FR-{{TAG}}-004 | A change from Program to Operator shows a confirm prompt that names the owning phase. | FAT-S |
| FR-{{TAG}}-005 | The module enters Out of Service only from Stopped. In Out of Service, the run output stays off. | FAT-S |
| FR-{{TAG}}-006 | The module executes transitions T1 to T9 as in Section 3.3, and no other transitions. | FAT-S: run each transition. Attempt each transition that is not listed. |
| FR-{{TAG}}-007 | Faulted latches until operator reset. The module never restarts automatically after a reset. | FAT-S |
| FR-{{TAG}}-008 | The batch system cannot reset a Faulted module. | FAT-S |

## 4. Regulatory control: speed

This module has no PID loop. The speed reference is open loop from the owner. {{If a loop exists, add: PV | output | action | mode behavior | cascade source.}}

| Item | Program | Operator |
|---|---|---|
| Speed reference source | Batch phase parameter {{name}} | Faceplate entry |
| Clamp | `SPD_MIN` to `SPD_MAX` | `SPD_MIN` to `SPD_MAX` |
| On mode change | Hold the last reference | Hold the last reference |
| During Starting | `SPD_START` | `SPD_START` |

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-{{TAG}}-009 | The module clamps the speed reference to `SPD_MIN` and `SPD_MAX` in all modes. It shows a clamp indication on the faceplate. | FAT-S: enter values outside the clamps. |
| FR-{{TAG}}-010 | During Starting, the module sends `SPD_START`. In Running, it sends the owner's reference. | FAT-S |
| FR-{{TAG}}-011 | The VFD applies the accel and decel ramps from its parameter file. The PLC does not ramp. | FAT-I: compare the VFD parameters with the parameter list. SAT-F: time a speed step. |

## 5. Sequences

### 5.1 Start (T1 → T2)

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Check all start permissives on the C&E chart | All healthy | None (evaluated once) | Reject the start. Show the missing permissive. Stay in Stopped. |
| S2 | Set the speed reference to `SPD_START`. Set the run command on. | Run feedback on | `START_TMO` | Run command off. Go to Faulted. Alarm: fail to start. |
| S3 | Wait `PROOF_DLY`. Enable the process trips that need flow. | Delay done | `PROOF_DLY` | Not applicable |
| S4 | Release the speed reference to the owner. Go to Running. | Done | None | Not applicable |

### 5.2 Stop (T4 → T5)

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | Set the run command off (VFD ramp stop) | Run feedback off | `STOP_TMO` | Go to Faulted. Alarm: fail to stop. Keep the run command off. |
| P2 | Go to Stopped | Done | None | Not applicable |

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-{{TAG}}-012 | The module executes the start sequence in Table 5.1, with the stated timeouts and failure responses. | FAT-S: simulate a missing permissive, missing feedback and normal feedback. |
| FR-{{TAG}}-013 | The module executes the stop sequence in Table 5.2, with the stated timeout and failure response. | FAT-S: simulate run feedback stuck on. |

## 6. Interlocks and permissives

The cause-and-effect chart {{doc}}, rows {{rows}}, defines all interlock and permissive logic. This narrative does not restate it.

Tags on the C&E chart for this module: {{list}}

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-{{TAG}}-014 | An interlock trip sets the run command off in all modes, including Operator, and sends the module to Faulted. | FAT-S, per C&E row |
| FR-{{TAG}}-015 | The faceplate shows the first-out trip cause until reset. | FAT-S |
| FR-{{TAG}}-016 | Bypass of an interlock or permissive is possible only as the control philosophy {{section}} defines. | FAT-S |

## 7. Alarms

The alarm database {{doc}} defines all alarms, priorities, limits and suppression. This narrative does not restate them.

The database must contain these module alarms: Fail to start, Fail to stop, Uncommanded stop, VFD fault, VFD comms loss, and the process alarms on {{tags}}.

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-{{TAG}}-017 | Each module alarm listed in Section 7 exists in the alarm database and activates as the database defines. | FAT-I: cross-check. FAT-S: activate each alarm. |

## 8. Abnormal conditions

| Condition | Detection | Response | Recovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bad PV on {{analog tag}} | Channel fault or out-of-range, per the I/O list | Per C&E row {{row}}. Show bad quality on the faceplate. | Automatic when the PV is good. Trip latch needs a reset. |
| Level switch wire break | Fail-safe wiring: wire break reads as the trip state | Same as a real trip | Reset after repair |
| PLC to VFD comms loss | Comms status bit | VFD stops on its comms-loss parameter. Module goes to Faulted. | Reset after comms return |
| Batch to PLC comms loss | {{detection}} | {{response}} | {{recovery}} |
| PLC power loss / restart | First scan | All outputs off. State goes to Stopped. Mode is retained. | Owner must send a new start |
| VFD power loss / return | Ready bit off | Module goes to Faulted. VFD auto-restart is disabled. | Operator reset |
| Local disconnect open | {{tag}} | Start permissive not met. If Running: uncommanded stop, Faulted. | Close the disconnect, then reset |
| Fail position | Not applicable | De-energized means stopped | Not applicable |

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-{{TAG}}-018 | The module responds to each condition in Table 8 as stated. | FAT-S for each row. SAT-F for wire break and power loss. |
| FR-{{TAG}}-019 | The module shows "Local disconnect open" as a status, separate from Faulted. | FAT-S |
| FR-{{TAG}}-020 | The VFD auto-restart and flying-start functions are disabled. | FAT-I: VFD parameter file. SAT-F: cycle VFD power while running. |

## 9. Operator interface

| Operator sees | Operator can change | Operator is prompted for |
|---|---|---|
| Mode, owner (phase name), state | Mode (confirm on Program → Operator) | Confirm mode change from Program |
| Speed reference, speed feedback, motor current | Start, Stop, speed (Operator mode only) | Confirm Out of Service |
| Permissive status, first-out trip | Reset (Faulted only) | Not applicable |
| {{process tags}} with quality | Not applicable | Not applicable |

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-{{TAG}}-021 | The faceplate shows and allows the items in Table 9, and nothing else. | FAT-S, with Operations witnessing |

## 10. Open items

| # | Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| {{n}} | {{item}} | {{name / role}} | {{YYYY-MM-DD}} |

# Part 2: Example, P-1102

```
CONTROL NARRATIVE: VFD PUMP P-1102
Doc no: {{DOC_NO}}    Rev: A    Class: VFD-PUMP rev 0
```

I do not have your document numbers, people or dates. Those fields stay as placeholders. Items I could not determine from your description are listed as open items, not guessed.

## 0. Document control

| Rev | Date | MOC no. | Description | By |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | {{YYYY-MM-DD}} | n/a | Issued for review | {{name}} |

**Deviations from the class standard:** None, until open items 1 to 6 are closed.

**References:** The same table as the template. SIS SRS: "Not applicable: no SIF on P-1102". Open item 6 confirms this.

## 1. Purpose and boundaries

- **Function:** P-1102 transfers product from mix tank T-110 to hold tank T-120.
- **Commanded by:** the T-110 Transfer phase, {{phase name}}.
- **Out of scope:** T-110 outlet valves and T-120 inlet valves (separate modules), CIP of the transfer line, and phase logic.

| Interface | Tag / module | Direction | Signal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Source | T-110 | In | LSL-110 |
| Destination | T-120 | In | LSH-120 |
| Batch system | {{Transfer phase}} | In / Out | Acquire, start, stop, speed reference, state, faults |
| VFD | {{VFD-1102}} | In / Out | {{network protocol}} (open item 4) |

## 2. Equipment and tags

| Role | Tag |
|---|---|
| Pump / motor | P-1102 |
| VFD | {{VFD-1102}} |
| Run command / run feedback | {{per I/O list}} |
| VFD fault / ready | {{per I/O list}} |
| Speed reference / speed feedback | {{per I/O list}} |
| Motor current | {{per I/O list}} |
| Local disconnect status | {{tag, or "Not monitored"}} |
| Discharge pressure | PT-1102 |
| Source low level | LSL-110 |
| Destination high level | LSH-120 |

**Parameter list entries:** `P1102.START_TMO`, `P1102.STOP_TMO`, `P1102.SPD_MIN`, `P1102.SPD_MAX`, `P1102.SPD_START`, `P1102.SW_DEBOUNCE`, `P1102.PROOF_DLY`. The VFD ramps are in the {{VFD-1102}} parameter file.

## 3. Modes and states

Sections 3.1 to 3.3 are the class standard, with no change.

Requirements FR-P1102-001 to FR-P1102-008 are the class text with `{{TAG}}` = P-1102. Example:

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-P1102-001 | In Program mode, P-1102 accepts start, stop and speed commands only from the T-110 Transfer phase. | FAT-S |
| FR-P1102-004 | A change from Program to Operator shows a confirm prompt that names the T-110 Transfer phase. | FAT-S |
| FR-P1102-007 | Faulted latches until operator reset. P-1102 never restarts automatically after a reset. | FAT-S |

## 4. Regulatory control: speed

There is no PID loop. In Program mode, the speed reference comes from the T-110 Transfer phase parameter {{name}}. PT-1102 is used for monitoring and interlocks only. It does not control speed.

FR-P1102-009 to FR-P1102-011 are the class text.

## 5. Sequences

Tables 5.1 and 5.2 are the class standard. For P-1102, step S3 enables the PT-1102 process checks that need flow (open item 2). FR-P1102-012 and FR-P1102-013 are the class text.

## 6. Interlocks and permissives

The C&E chart {{doc}}, rows {{rows}}, defines all logic for P-1102.

Tags on the C&E chart for P-1102:
- LSL-110: T-110 low level. Dry-run protection.
- LSH-120: T-120 high level. Overfill protection.
- PT-1102: discharge pressure. Trip type is open item 1.

FR-P1102-014 to FR-P1102-016 are the class text.

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-P1102-022 | LSL-110 and LSH-120 are wired fail-safe. A wire break reads as the trip state. | SAT-F: open the loop at the field junction box. P-1102 trips. |
| FR-P1102-023 | LSL-110 and LSH-120 apply `P1102.SW_DEBOUNCE` before they cause a trip. | FAT-S: pulse the input shorter and longer than the debounce. |

## 7. Alarms

The alarm database {{doc}} must contain:
- P-1102 Fail to start, Fail to stop, Uncommanded stop, VFD fault, VFD comms loss.
- PT-1102 process alarms.
- LSL-110 and LSH-120 alarms, if these exist in the database. They may belong to the tank modules.

FR-P1102-017 is the class text.

## 8. Abnormal conditions

The rows are the class standard, with these entries:

| Condition | Response for P-1102 |
|---|---|
| Bad PV on PT-1102 | Per C&E row {{row}}. Open item 3 decides alarm-only or trip. |
| LSL-110 / LSH-120 wire break | P-1102 trips (FR-P1102-022) |
| Batch to PLC comms loss | Open item 5 |

FR-P1102-018 to FR-P1102-020 are the class text.

## 9. Operator interface

The class standard, with PT-1102, LSL-110 and LSH-120 shown on the faceplate with their quality. FR-P1102-021 is the class text. Operations must sign this section.

## 10. Open items

| # | Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Confirm the pump type (centrifugal or positive displacement). For PD, define the PT-1102 high-pressure trip and the relief arrangement. This is deadhead protection when a downstream valve is closed. | Process | {{YYYY-MM-DD}} |
| 2 | Decide whether low PT-1102 after `PROOF_DLY` is a loss-of-prime trip. If yes, add it to the C&E chart. | Process | {{YYYY-MM-DD}} |
| 3 | Define the response to bad PV on PT-1102: alarm only, or trip. | Process + Controls | {{YYYY-MM-DD}} |
| 4 | Confirm the VFD network protocol and the comms-loss stop mode (ramp or coast). | Controls | {{YYYY-MM-DD}} |
| 5 | Define the P-1102 response to batch-to-PLC comms loss. Options: hold state and speed, or stop. Align this with the phase hold behavior. | Controls + Operations | {{YYYY-MM-DD}} |
| 6 | Confirm that no SIF exists on P-1102 (no hazard beyond equipment damage and product loss). | Process Safety | {{YYYY-MM-DD}} |
| 7 | Define P-1102 behavior during CIP. Is LSL-110 active or bypassed? Who owns the speed? This may need a CIP mode or a separate CIP phase reference. | Process + QA | {{YYYY-MM-DD}} |
| 8 | Confirm whether LSL-110 and LSH-120 are hardwired into the VFD enable, through the PLC, or both. | Controls | {{YYYY-MM-DD}} |

| Every state has entry permissives and exits | Met (Table 3.2) |
| Every sequence step has a timeout and failure response | Met. Steps without a timeout are marked "None" or "Not applicable". |

| SIS | Referenced. Open item 6 confirms. |

**Suggested next step:** use the same skeleton for the other three classes (on/off valve, modulating valve, agitator). The modulating valve is the one class where Section 4 needs real loop content.
